title: AI-Assisted Employee Onboarding
built: Integrated midPoint, Active Directory and Keycloak with local peer-based access recommendations and Ollama explanations; native policy and approvals control every grant.
problem: Reduce incorrect onboarding recommendations while preserving deterministic least-privilege enforcement and independent approval.
objective: Validate a complete HR-to-directory-to-application onboarding workflow using synthetic enterprise data.
outcome: All 20 hires were provisioned and passed AD authentication, browser sign-in, allowed department access and denied cross-department access. Approval/rejection, duplicate replay and live partial-failure recovery passed. On this controlled fixture, recommendation accuracy increased from 89% to 100%; both policy-enforced paths had zero excessive grants.
steps: Use the [extended reference](REFERENCE.md) for native configuration, integration contract and measurement limits.

tests.check: Historical enterprise employees in both targets
Valid hires provisioned with exact independent expected access

tests.expected: No preapproval grants; requester 403; distinct reviewer decisions; browser 200/403

tests.check: Real partial-target outage and native recovery
tests.expected: 503 with existing AD identity; recovery creates/links correct Keycloak identity

problems: Native group references and explicitly fetched Keycloak groups were necessary for correct reconciliation.
Approval rules needed explicit assignment-level scope; actual target revocation and pending-state denial were verified.
An exact role-ID allowlist prevents administrative roles from entering the request catalog.

limitations: Controlled synthetic workload with deliberately matching peer categories and coarse RBAC baseline. No production speedup, human review-time saving or broader model generalization established. Full independent manual replay remains untested; original integration is not distributed.
overview_limitations: Controlled synthetic workload; AI added latency. Human review-time savings, broader generalization and a complete fresh manual replay were not established. The original integration is not distributed; conventional configuration and adapter requirements are documented.
